docs.title: AspectK
docs.text:
Compile-time Aspect-Oriented Programming for Kotlin Multiplatform.

AspectK is a Kotlin compiler plugin that injects advice into your functions at compile time. There is no runtime reflection and no proxy. Declare an @Aspect, mark its advice with @Before, @After or @Around, and the calls are compiled into every function that carries the target annotation.

docs.title: Why AspectK?
docs.text:
• Compile-Time Injection

    Advice is injected during K2 IR transformation, with no reflection and no dynamic proxies. The generated code is what you would get by writing the calls by hand.

  • Kotlin Multiplatform

    Runs on JVM, JS, WASM and Native. An aspect defined in commonMain applies on every target.

  • K2 IR

    Built on the K2 compiler's IR API. Supports Kotlin 2.2.20 through 2.4.10.

docs.title: 1. Add the plugin
docs.text:
// build.gradle.kts
plugins {
    id("io.github.mole-labs.aspectk") version "LATEST_VERSION"
}

The plugin adds aspectk-runtime for you, so there is no dependency to declare.

docs.title: 2. Define a target annotation
docs.text:
@Target(AnnotationTarget.FUNCTION)
@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
annotation class Logged

docs.title: 3. Create an Aspect
docs.text:
@Aspect
object LoggingAspect {
    @Before(target = [Logged::class])
    fun log(joinPoint: JoinPoint) {
        println("→ ${joinPoint.signature.methodName}(${joinPoint.args.joinToString()})")
    }
}

docs.title: 4. Annotate your functions
docs.text:
@Logged
fun processOrder(orderId: String, amount: Double) {
    // AspectK injects LoggingAspect.log() here at compile time
    println("Processing order $orderId")
}

docs.title: IR Transformation Pipeline
docs.text:
1. K2 calls AdviceGenerationExtension.generate() once per module
  2. AspectVisitor scans the IR for @Aspect objects and fills AspectLookUp
  3. Hints from earlier builds and from upstream modules are merged into AspectLookUp
  4. InheritableVisitor records overrides for advice declared with inherits = true
  5. AspectTransformer walks every function and injects advice into the ones that match
  6. The generators (MethodSignatureGenerator, JoinPointGenerator, ProceedingJoinPointGenerator, AdviceCallGenerator) produce the IR nodes

The architecture overview covers each stage in detail. To add a new advice type, start from AspectTransformer and AdviceCallGenerator.

docs.title: AOP Overview
docs.text: Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) separates cross-cutting concerns from business logic. A cross-cutting concern is code that many unrelated functions need, such as logging, authentication or metrics.

docs.title: The Problem: Cross-Cutting Concerns
docs.text:
Without AOP, the same lines are repeated in every function:

fun processPayment(amount: Double, userId: String) {
    logger.info("processPayment called")     // logging
    checkAuthenticated(userId)               // auth
    metrics.increment("payment.calls")       // metrics
    // --- actual business logic ---
    chargeCard(amount, userId)
}

fun refundPayment(paymentId: String) {
    logger.info("refundPayment called")      // logging (again)
    checkAuthenticated(userId)               // auth (again)
    metrics.increment("refund.calls")        // metrics (again)
    // --- actual business logic ---
    reverseCharge(paymentId)
}

docs.title: The AspectK Solution
docs.text:
With AspectK, each concern lives in one aspect and the functions only carry annotations:

// Business logic
@Logged @Authenticated @Metered
fun processPayment(amount: Double, userId: String) {
    chargeCard(amount, userId)
}

@Logged @Authenticated @Metered
fun refundPayment(paymentId: String) {
    reverseCharge(paymentId)
}

// The logging concern, in one place
@Aspect
object LoggingAspect {
    @Before(target = [Logged::class])
    fun log(jp: JoinPoint) = logger.info("${jp.signature.methodName} called")
}

docs.title: Why not AspectJ?
docs.text:
AspectJ can express more than any other AOP framework on the JVM, and its pointcut expression language is where the cost shows up:

// AspectJ — string-based pointcut expression
@Aspect
public class LoggingAspect {
    @Before("execution(* com.example.service.*.*(..)) && " +
            "@annotation(com.example.Logged) && " +
            "within(com.example..*)")
    public void log(JoinPoint jp) { ... }
}

Problems with this approach:

  • Pointcuts are plain strings. A typo compiles fine and only shows up when the advice silently fails to apply.
  • Renaming a class or method doesn't update the pointcut string.
  • The expression language (execution(), within(), args() and so on) takes time to learn.
  • AspectJ works on JVM bytecode, so it cannot target Kotlin Multiplatform.

docs.title: AspectK: Type-Safe Pointcuts
docs.text:
AspectK uses KClass references instead of strings, so the compiler checks every pointcut:

// AspectK — type-safe, no strings, no runtime container
@Aspect
object LoggingAspect {
    @Before(target = [Logged::class])  // KClass reference, not a string
    fun log(jp: JoinPoint) { ... }
}
AspectJ AspectK Pointcut definition String expression KClass reference Type-safe? ❌ No ✅ Yes Refactor-safe? ❌ No ✅ Yes Runtime dependency ❌ No (weave-time) ❌ No KMP support ❌ JVM only ✅ All targets

The target parameter takes KClass<out Annotation> references. Rename an annotation class and the IDE updates every aspect that references it. Delete one and those aspects stop compiling.

docs.title: How Injection Works: Before vs After Compilation
docs.text: AspectK uses the K2 IR (Intermediate Representation) transformation API. After your source is parsed and type-checked, the compiler plugin walks the IR tree and inserts advice calls into the matching function bodies.

docs.title: Before Compilation (your source code)
docs.text:
@Target(AnnotationTarget.FUNCTION)
@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
annotation class Logged

@Aspect
object LoggingAspect {
    @Before(target = [Logged::class])
    fun log(joinPoint: JoinPoint) {
        println("→ ${joinPoint.signature.methodName}(${joinPoint.args.joinToString()})")
    }
}

class OrderService {
    @Logged
    fun placeOrder(orderId: String, amount: Double) {
        println("Order placed: $orderId, $amount")
    }
}

docs.title: After IR Transformation (equivalent generated code)
docs.text:
The plugin rewrites placeOrder so that the advice call is the first statement of the body:

// You don't write this. It shows what the compiler generates.
// AspectK generates the names containing `$`, which is why they are backtick-quoted here.

class OrderService {
    // Generated by AspectK: synthetic inner object holding compile-time metadata,
    // initialized once per class load (not per call).
    private object `$MethodSignatures` {
        val `ajc$tjp_0`: MethodSignature = MethodSignature(
            methodName = "placeOrder",
            annotations = listOf(
                AnnotationInfo(Logged::class, "com.example.Logged", emptyList(), emptyList()),
            ),
            parameter = listOf(
                // The dispatch receiver (this) is always the first entry
                MethodParameter("<this>", OrderService::class, "com.example.OrderService", emptyList(), false),
                MethodParameter("orderId", String::class, "kotlin.String", emptyList(), false),
                MethodParameter("amount",  Double::class, "kotlin.Double", emptyList(), false),
            ),
            returnType = Unit::class,
            returnTypeName = "kotlin.Unit",
        )
    }

    fun placeOrder(orderId: String, amount: Double) {
        // ↓ Injected by AspectK at compile time
        LoggingAspect.log(
            DefaultJoinPoint(
                target    = this,
                signature = `$MethodSignatures`.`ajc$tjp_0`,
                // args[0] is always the dispatch receiver (this) for member functions,
                // followed by the declared value parameters in order
                args      = listOf(this, orderId, amount),
            )
        )
        // ↓ Original function body, unchanged
        println("Order placed: $orderId, $amount")
    }
}

docs.title: What to notice
docs.text:
• The @Before advice call is the first statement of the transformed body. It is a direct function call, with no wrapper and no proxy object.
  • MethodSignature is initialized once per class load, not once per call. AspectK generates a synthetic object $MethodSignatures inside the containing class, with one property per intercepted function (ajc$tjp_0, ajc$tjp_1, …).
  • For member functions, JoinPoint.args starts with the dispatch receiver (this), followed by the value parameters in declaration order. Top-level functions have no dispatch receiver, so args holds only the value parameters and target is null.
  • MethodSignature.parameter has the same layout as JoinPoint.args. For member functions the first entry is the <this> receiver parameter.
  • @Before leaves the original body as it is and only prepends to it. @After wraps the body in try/finally, and @Around moves it into a lambda. See @After and @Around.
  • The generated code is ordinary Kotlin and needs no framework at runtime beyond the small aspectk-runtime library that defines JoinPoint and its related classes.
